# Baaton

> Your agents did the work. Now prove it.
> Every agent run can be published as a receipt signed with Ed25519 — anyone can verify it
> against your org's public keys, without trusting you or us.

## Who it's for
- You run more than one product and several coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw).
- You bill, report or answer for work your agents produced, and need an artifact that holds up.
- Your cofounder, client or teammate is not an engineer and still has to read what happened.

## Why not Linear, Jira or GitHub
They are built for a team of humans that lives in the tool, with agents added as extra
teammates alongside them. Baaton inverts it: agents are the primary writers over the API,
humans read and decide. And when a run ends, Baaton emits something none of them do —
a cryptographically signed receipt of what the agent did.

A customer starts the ticket. The team and the agent continue it internally.
The run comes back as a verifiable artifact you can hand to whoever paid for it.

## How it works
1. A request arrives: a public intake form, an inbound-email webhook, or your own API call.
2. Your team shapes the ticket: brief, acceptance criteria, images, attachments.
3. Your agent pulls the full project context in one API call, does the work, posts a TLDR
   with files changed and test status.
4. Publish the run. You get a Run Card at `r.baaton.dev/<token>` and a signed
   `receipt.json` that a third party can verify against your org's JWKS.

API-first: one curl opens an issue. 198 endpoints, no SDK required.

## Verify a receipt yourself
No account needed. Signature is Ed25519 (EdDSA), keys are per-organization,
receipts follow the [agent-receipts protocol](https://agentreceipts.ai).

```bash
# 1. Fetch a published run receipt
curl -s https://api.baaton.dev/api/v1/public/runs/<token>/receipt.json

# 2. Fetch the issuing org's public keys
curl -s https://api.baaton.dev/api/v1/public/orgs/<org_id>/jwks.json

# 3. Verify signature.value over the exact bytes served in step 1
#    (alg: EdDSA, kid matches the JWKS entry, kty: OKP, crv: Ed25519)
```

Verify against the exact bytes returned by the API. Re-serializing the JSON before
verifying will change the bytes and the check will fail.

## URLs
- Website: https://baaton.dev
- App: https://app.baaton.dev
- API Base: https://api.baaton.dev/api/v1
- Public API Docs (Markdown): https://api.baaton.dev/api/v1/public/docs
- Agent Skill (SKILL.md): https://api.baaton.dev/api/v1/public/skill
- Full API Reference: https://baaton.dev/llms-full.txt

## API Authentication
```
Authorization: Bearer baa_yo…here
```
Keys are issued per organization, with optional project-level scoping so a key can be
restricted to specific projects.

## Response Format
All responses: `{ "data": ... }`. Errors: `{ "error": "message", "field": "...", "accepted_values": [...] }`.
Core agent endpoints (issues, projects, comments, TLDRs, sprints, milestones, webhooks,
agent sessions) include `_hints` with recommended next actions.

## Core Endpoints (198 total)

### Proof: signed receipts for agent work
- POST /agent-sessions — Open a run (issue_id, agent_name, agent_id)
- POST /agent-sessions/{id}/steps — Append a step as the agent works
- GET /agent-sessions/{id}/stream — SSE live stream of steps
- POST /agent-sessions/{id}/publish — Publish the run as a shareable Run Card
- GET /public/runs/{token} — Read-only Run Card. No auth.
- GET /public/runs/{token}/receipt.json — Ed25519-signed receipt for that run. No auth.
- GET /public/orgs/{org_id}/jwks.json — Org public keys to verify receipts. No auth.

### Collect: requests from people without an account
- POST /public/{slug}/submit — Client-facing intake form. No auth. Creates an issue.
- POST /public/{slug}/email-intake — Webhook endpoint that turns an inbound email into an
  issue. Requires email intake enabled on the project and an upstream email provider
  posting to it.
- GET /public/resolve/{token} — Resolve a shareable project link.
- GET /public/docs — Full API docs as Markdown. No auth.
- GET /public/skill — Agent SKILL.md. No auth.

### Projects & Issues
- GET /projects — List projects
- GET /projects/{id}/context — Full project context in one call (for agents)
- POST /issues — Create issue (project_id, title, priority, status, issue_type)
- GET /issues — List issues (?project_id, ?status, ?priority, ?assignee_id, ?label, ?search)
- PATCH /issues/{id} — Update issue
- DELETE /issues/{id} — Delete issue
- PATCH /issues/batch — Bulk update (ids[], updates{})
- DELETE /issues/batch — Bulk delete (ids[])
- GET /issues/mine — My assigned issues
- POST /issues/{id}/comments — Add comment
- POST /issues/{id}/tldr — Post agent summary (TLDR) with files changed and test status

### Search
- GET /search?q= — Project-scoped full-text search
- GET /search/global?q= — Cross-org search (all user orgs)

### Automations & Webhooks
- GET /projects/{id}/automations — List automations
- POST /projects/{id}/automations — Create automation (trigger, conditions[], actions[])
- POST /webhooks — Create webhook (url, events[]) — HMAC signed

### AI
- POST /ai/chat — AI chat (messages[], model?, tools?)
- GET /billing/ai-usage — Token usage report (from, to)

### Other
- Milestones, Sprints, Cycles, Initiatives, Labels, Templates, Recurring Issues, SLA Rules,
  Views, Notifications, Attachments, Custom Fields, Relations, GitHub Integration,
  Slack Integration, Agent Config

## Enums
- Priority: urgent | high | medium | low
- Issue Type: bug | feature | improvement | question
- Status: per-project (default: backlog, todo, in_progress, in_review, done, cancelled)

## Webhook Events
issue.created, issue.updated, issue.deleted, status.changed, comment.created, comment.deleted

## Agent Quick Start
```bash
export BAATON_API_KEY=***
export BAATON_BASE_URL=https://api.baaton.dev/api/v1

# Get docs (no auth needed)
curl -s $BAATON_BASE_URL/public/docs

# List projects
curl -s $BAATON_BASE_URL/projects -H "Authorization: Bearer $BAATON_API_KEY"

# Create issue
curl -s -X POST $BAATON_BASE_URL/issues \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BAATON_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_id":"...","title":"Fix bug","priority":"high"}'

# Open a run, then publish it as a signed receipt
curl -s -X POST $BAATON_BASE_URL/agent-sessions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BAATON_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"issue_id":"...","agent_name":"claude-code"}'
```

## Built on Baaton
Baaton is developed on Baaton. Snapshot of the production board on 2026-08-23:
17 projects and 541 issues, most of them written by coding agents over the API.

## Pricing
- Free ($0): 2 users, 1 org, 3 projects, 500 issues, 1K API/mo, 50 AI messages/mo
- Pro ($19/mo, 3 users included, +$19/extra): 5 orgs, 25 projects, unlimited issues, 100K API/mo, 2K AI messages/mo, BYOK, webhooks, automations, agent config
- Enterprise (on demand): Unlimited everything, SAML/SCIM, self-hosted, SLA
